title: Access after cancellation
text:
Title: Access after cancellation

Category: billing

Content:
# Access after cancellation

When a paid ExampleOps plan is cancelled, access usually continues until the end of the current billing period.

This means your team may still be able to use paid features after cancellation. This is expected behavior and does not mean the cancellation failed. The exact access end date is shown on the billing settings page.

At the end of the billing period, the workspace moves to the free plan. Features that are not included in the free plan may stop working. Existing data remains in the workspace, but some actions may be limited until the plan is upgraded again.

Access after cancellation is different from a failed payment restriction. A cancelled plan stays active until the scheduled end date. A failed payment may restrict access earlier if the invoice remains unpaid after retry attempts.

title: Billing permissions
text:
Title: Billing permissions

Category: billing

Content:
# Billing permissions

Billing settings are only available to workspace owners and users with billing admin permissions.

Users with billing permissions can view invoices, update payment methods, change plans and cancel subscriptions. Regular members cannot manage billing settings unless their role is changed.

If the previous billing admin left the company, a workspace owner can assign billing permissions to another user. If no active owner is available, contact ExampleOps support for account recovery steps.

Billing permissions are separate from general workspace access. A user may be able to use the workspace but not manage billing. A user may also be a billing admin without being responsible for every workspace setting.

If your team is locked out after a payment issue, billing permissions alone may not fix the problem. Check failed payment, workspace access and entitlement sync information.

title: Cancel your plan
text:
Title: Cancel your plan

Category: billing

Content:
# Cancel your plan

Workspace owners can cancel an ExampleOps subscription from the billing settings page.

When you cancel a paid plan, the cancellation is scheduled for the end of the current billing period. Your workspace can usually continue using paid features until that date. The workspace is not deleted when the plan is cancelled.

After the billing period ends, the workspace moves to the free plan. Some paid features may become unavailable, including advanced exports, higher usage limits, premium integrations and some admin controls.

Cancelling a plan does not automatically issue a refund. Refund eligibility depends on the refund policy and the timing of the cancellation.

Only users with billing permissions can cancel a plan. If you cannot see the cancellation option, ask a workspace owner or billing admin to check your role.

title: Download invoices
text:
Title: Download invoices

Category: billing

Content:
# Download invoices

Workspace owners and billing admins can download invoices from the billing settings page.

Each invoice includes the billing period, amount charged, payment status, tax details and the payment method used. Paid invoices can be downloaded as PDF files.

If an invoice is marked as open or unpaid, the payment may still be processing or may have failed. Check the failed payment article for steps related to payment collection.

Invoice access depends on your workspace role. If you cannot see invoices, ask a workspace owner or billing admin to update your permissions.

Downloading an invoice does not change plan access, payment status or workspace permissions. If your team cannot access the workspace after payment, the issue may be related to workspace access or entitlement sync rather than the invoice itself.

title: Failed payment
text:
Title: Failed payment

Category: billing

Content:
# Failed payment

If a payment fails, ExampleOps will show a billing warning to workspace owners and billing admins.

Common reasons for failed payments include expired cards, insufficient funds, bank declines, authentication requirements and payment method restrictions.

ExampleOps may retry the payment automatically. During the retry period, your workspace may continue to have access to paid features. If the invoice remains unpaid, access to some paid features may be restricted.

A failed payment is not the same as cancelling a plan. Cancellation is requested by a user and usually takes effect at the end of the billing period. Failed payment restrictions happen when an invoice cannot be collected.

If your invoice is marked as paid but your team still cannot access the workspace, check workspace access and entitlement sync information. The issue may not be a payment failure.

title: Refund policy
text:
Title: Refund policy

Category: billing

Content:
# Refund policy

Cancelling an ExampleOps plan does not automatically create a refund.

Refunds are reviewed based on the type of charge, the timing of the request and whether the paid plan was used during the billing period. Monthly subscriptions are usually not refunded after the billing period has started.

If you believe a charge was made in error, contact support with your workspace name, invoice number and the reason for the refund request.

Refund requests are separate from cancellation requests. Cancelling prevents future renewal charges, while a refund request asks ExampleOps to review a past charge.

If your team still has access after cancelling, that does not always mean a refund is owed. Access usually continues until the end of the paid billing period.

title: Export dashboard data
text:
Title: Export dashboard data

Category: exports

Content:
# Export dashboard data

ExampleOps allows users with export permissions to export dashboard data as a CSV file.

Exports include the data visible from the selected dashboard, based on the current workspace and report configuration. Large exports may take longer to generate.

Dashboard exports are different from invoices. Billing invoices are downloaded from billing settings, while dashboard data exports are created from reporting pages.

Some plans include export limits. If the export option is unavailable, check your plan limits and export permissions.

If you need to export only the rows matching active filters, use filtered exports instead of exporting the full dashboard data.

title: Export filtered results
text:
Title: Export filtered results

Category: exports

Content:
# Export filtered results

Filtered exports allow users to download only the rows that match the filters currently applied to a dashboard or report.

Before exporting, apply the filters you want to use. ExampleOps will generate a CSV file based on the filtered result set rather than the full dashboard.

Filtered exports are useful when you need a subset of customers, workflows, tickets or activity records.

If the export includes more rows than expected, check whether the filters were applied before starting the export.

Filtered exports require export permissions and may be affected by plan limits. If you cannot export filtered results, review export permissions and plan limits.

title: Export permissions
text:
Title: Export permissions

Category: exports

Content:
# Export permissions

Export permissions control which users can download dashboard and report data from ExampleOps.

Workspace owners and admins can grant export access from the member settings page. Some roles can view dashboards but cannot export data.

If a user cannot see the export button, confirm their workspace role and export permission settings.

Export permissions are separate from billing permissions. A user may be allowed to manage invoices but not export customer or report data. A user may also be able to use the workspace but not download data.

If export permissions look correct but the export is still unavailable, check plan limits and browser troubleshooting information.

title: Downgrade your plan
text:
Title: Downgrade your plan

Category: plans

Content:
# Downgrade your plan

Workspace owners and billing admins can downgrade an ExampleOps plan from the plan settings page.

A downgrade is usually scheduled for the end of the current billing period. Until then, the workspace may continue to use the current paid features and limits.

After the downgrade takes effect, features and limits from the higher plan may no longer be available. Existing data remains in the workspace, but some actions may be limited until the plan is upgraded again.

Downgrading a plan is different from cancelling a subscription. Cancellation moves the workspace to the free plan at the end of the billing period. Downgrading moves the workspace to a lower paid plan.

Downgrading does not automatically create a refund. Refund requests are reviewed separately.

title: Plan limits
text:
Title: Plan limits

Category: plans

Content:
# Plan limits

Each ExampleOps plan includes limits for workspaces, projects, team members, exports, integrations and automation runs.

If your team cannot add more projects, invite more members or create additional workflows, you may have reached a plan limit. The current limit and usage count are shown on the plan settings page.

Plan limits are different from billing access issues. A workspace can have an active paid plan and still be blocked from creating more resources if the current plan limit has been reached.

Upgrading increases available limits for future usage. Downgrading may reduce limits at the end of the billing period.

If a feature is unavailable after a payment or subscription change, review entitlement sync information as well as the plan limits page.

title: Upgrade your plan
text:
Title: Upgrade your plan

Category: plans

Content:
# Upgrade your plan

Workspace owners and billing admins can upgrade an ExampleOps plan from the plan settings page.

Upgrading can increase limits for projects, team members, exports, integrations and automation runs. Some advanced features are only available on higher plans.

When a plan is upgraded, the billing change is applied to the workspace and entitlements may take a short time to sync. If the invoice is paid but new limits are not available yet, review entitlement sync information.

Only users with billing permissions can upgrade a plan. Regular workspace members cannot change subscription level.

If your team needs more capacity because you reached a limit, upgrading may be the correct action. If you cannot access an existing workspace, review workspace access instead.

title: Change workspace admin role
text:
Title: Change workspace admin role

Category: workspace

Content:
# Change workspace admin role

Workspace owners can promote members to admin roles from the member management page.

Admins can manage workspace membership, invitations and some workspace settings, but billing permissions may still be separate depending on the assigned role.

If an admin left the company, a workspace owner should assign a replacement admin to maintain access and workspace management continuity.

If nobody can manage the workspace because the previous admin or owner is unavailable, contact ExampleOps support for recovery steps.

Changing a workspace admin role does not automatically resolve billing sync or payment-related access issues. If access changed after a billing event, review failed payment and entitlement sync information as well.

title: Entitlement sync after billing changes
text:
Title: Entitlement sync after billing changes

Category: workspace

Content:
# Entitlement sync after billing changes

ExampleOps uses entitlement sync to apply billing and plan changes to workspace access and feature availability.

When a payment succeeds, fails or a subscription changes, billing status and workspace entitlements may take a short time to sync. During this period, a workspace may show a paid invoice while some users still cannot access paid features or expected limits.

If a workspace remains out of sync after a billing update, a workspace owner should confirm the latest billing status, wait for the sync window to complete and then contact support if access is still incorrect.

Entitlement sync issues are different from invitation or role problems. If only one user cannot access the workspace, review workspace membership and role configuration first.

If the whole workspace is affected after a payment or subscription change, entitlement sync is a more likely cause than individual user access settings.

title: Invite team members
text:
Title: Invite team members

Category: workspace

Content:
# Invite team members

Workspace owners and admins can invite new team members from the workspace settings page.

Each invite is tied to an email address. To avoid access problems, make sure the invited user signs in with the same email address that received the invitation.

If a user says they cannot access the workspace, confirm whether they accepted the invite, used the correct email address and joined the intended workspace.

Inviting a team member does not automatically grant billing permissions. Billing settings, invoices and payment methods are still limited to workspace owners and billing admins.

If the user was invited successfully but paid features are still unavailable after a billing change, review entitlement sync information.

title: Troubleshoot workspace access
text:
Title: Troubleshoot workspace access

Category: workspace

Content:
# Troubleshoot workspace access

If a user cannot access an ExampleOps workspace, first confirm that they were invited to the correct workspace and accepted the invitation with the expected email address.

Workspace access issues can happen when a user was removed from the workspace, accepted an invite with the wrong email address, signed in through the wrong authentication method or does not have the required role.

If only some users are affected, ask a workspace owner or admin to review the member list and confirm the affected users still appear as active members.

If the workspace recently changed plan status or had a payment issue, access to some features may depend on entitlement sync. In those cases, review entitlement sync information in addition to billing status.

Workspace access is different from billing permissions. A user may be able to use the workspace but still be unable to manage billing, invoices or payment methods.
